curated.category: 恶性肿瘤 / 消化道末端HPV相关鳞癌
curated.lethality_detail_zh: 约85%–90%为鳞状细胞癌且高度与高危型HPV（主要为HPV16）感染相关，早期常仅表现为无痛性便血、肛门坠胀或触及肿物，极易被当成“痔疮”或肛裂长期自行涂药膏而延误；总体慢性进展，晚期可致肠梗阻、直肠阴道瘘或盆腔大出血。
curated.treatability_summary_zh: 与直肠腺癌治疗策略截然不同！肛管鳞癌对同步放化疗极度敏感，绝大多数非转移患者（Ⅰ–Ⅲ期）无需切肛门改道，首选“丝裂霉素+5-FU/卡培他滨联合调强放疗(Nigro方案)”即可获得70%–85%的5年生存率且成功保留肛门括约肌功能；仅放化疗后残留/复发者才需挽救性腹会阴联合切除(APR)。

annual_deaths_global.range_or_note: 2022年全球约2.18万例死亡，女性发病略高于男性（约1.5–2:1），HIV阳性及免疫抑制人群发病率显著升高

annual_deaths_china.range_or_note: GLOBOCAN与NCC常规报告通常将肛管癌并入结直肠癌大类统计，未单独拆分中国独立死亡人数；相对结直肠癌属少见瘤种
annual_deaths_china.source: IARC GLOBOCAN 2022 / CSCO结直肠癌及肛管癌诊疗规范

clinical_management.acute_emergency_protocol_zh: 1) 肿瘤巨大堵塞肛管致完全性急性低位肠梗阻（停止排气排便、剧烈腹胀呕吐）：立即禁食胃肠减压并急诊行腹腔镜横结肠或乙状结肠造口术解除梗阻，切勿急诊强行切除肛管肿瘤，待造口后顺利完成同步放化疗; 2) 肿瘤破溃致肛门活动性大出血：压迫止血、输血扩容并急诊放疗止血或介入栓塞。

non_drug_therapies_zh: 初诊切忌误诊为‘痔疮’行盲目痔疮切除，直肠指检与肛门镜活检明确病理为鳞癌后，首要选择是根治性同步放化疗保肛而非直接手术切肛
同步放化疗结束后需耐心等待8–26周再评估肿瘤是否完全消退（肛管癌放疗后退缩缓慢，切忌在8周内过早判定失败而盲目切肛）

research_progress.breakthroughs_and_trials_zh: 1) 3期POD1UM-303研究(ESMO 2024)证实PD-1单抗Retifanlimab联合卡铂+紫杉醇一线治疗局部复发/转移性肛管鳞癌显著延长无进展生存(9.3 vs 7.4个月)并有总生存获益趋势，确立免疫联合化疗新标准; 2) PLATO英国伞式试验正根据T1–T4分期精准探索低危小肿瘤降剂量放疗减毒与高危局部晚期加量巩固; 3) 循环HPV-ctDNA液体活检可在放化疗后提前数月极高灵敏度预测局部复发。
research_progress.key_unmet_needs_zh: 1) 患者与部分基层医生长期将早期症状误认为‘痔疮’，延误甚至误行不规范局部手术; 2) 同步放化疗导致的急性放射性皮炎/直肠炎及远期肛门括约肌纤维化失禁、性功能障碍影响生活质量; 3) 转移及放化疗后复发患者缺乏国内已正式获批纳入常规报销的免疫/ADC药物。

master.definition_en: A hamartomatous polyp that occurs in the stomach, small and large intestines, and rarely within the esophagus, nasopharynx and the urinary tract. The Peutz-Jeghers polyps are grossly lobulated and dark. Microscopically, they have a central core of smooth muscle covered by mucosa. The smooth muscle shows tree-like branching. The question of whether or not the Peutz-Jeghers polyp is precancerous is a matter of controversy. The loss of heterozygosity on chromosome 19p (where the responsible gene LKB1 is located) suggests that the increased risk of malignancy may be due to malignant transformation from hamartoma to adenocarcinoma. --2002

master.definition_en: A rare common cystic lymphatic malformation characterized by a benign cystic lesion composed of dilated lymphatic channels. Mixed cystic lesions consist of cysts both larger (macrocystic) and smaller (microcystic) than 1 cm in diameter. They usually present at birth or during the first years of life and most often occur in the head and neck region but may affect any site. Symptoms depend on the location and extent of the lesion. Infection, trauma, or intracystic hemorrhage can lead to lesional expansion. Malignant transformation does not occur.

master.definition_en: Aortic valve stenosis (AVS) is a condition characterized by narrowing of the heart's aortic valve opening. This narrowing prevents the valve from opening fully, which obstructs blood flow from the heart into the aorta, and onward to the rest of the body. AVS can range from mild to severe. Signs and symptoms typically develop when the narrowing of the opening is severe and may include chest pain (angina) or tightness; shortness of breath or fatigue (especially during exertion); feeling faint or fainting; heart palpitations; and heart murmur. Individuals with less severe congenital AVS (present at birth) may not develop symptoms until adulthood. Individuals with severe cases may faint without warning. AVS can have several causes including abnormal development before birth (such as having 1 or 2 valve leaflets instead of 3); calcium build-up on the valve in adulthood; and rheumatic fever.

master.definition_en: A rare autoinflammatory syndrome with immune deficiency characterized by recurrent infections (bacterial and viral) due to NCKAP1L mutations. Patients are present with recurrent respiratory tract infections and recurrent pneumonia mostly causing bronchiectasis, bacteremia, and meningitis. Patients also have systemic hyperinflammation which mostly presents with an atopic disease, hepatosplenomegaly, and lymphoproliferation. Cytokine overproduction, antibody abnormalities, elevated IgE levels and increased B cells are observed.

master.definition_en: A rare acquired pituitary hormone deficieny characterized by inflammation of the pituitary gland secondary to immunotherapy for cancers treatments (such as monoclonal antibodies against cytotoxic T lymphocytes antigen, programmed cell death protein-1, and programmed cell death ligand molecules). Major clinical features include headache, fatigue, adrenal insufficiency and hypothyroidism. Patients may also have nausea and vomiting associated to the headache as well as dizziness and hot flashes. Enlargement of the pituitary gland is present in the brain imaging.
